title: Next-Word Prediction and Temperature
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Predict what the temperature setting does to a language model's choice of the next word, then reveal the adjusted probabilities and a draw of 20 sampled words, for four illustrative prompts.

educational.topic: Next-word prediction, softmax temperature, and sampling in large language models
learningObjectives: Infer how changing the temperature changes which next word a language model chooses and how often, answering at least 4 of 5 prediction questions correctly before the sampled results are revealed.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-reveal: the learner commits to an answer about the effect of temperature before the adjusted probabilities and a sampled draw of 20 are shown; free exploration follows
keyQuestions: At temperature 0, will the model ever choose a word other than the favorite?
What does a higher temperature do to the least likely word?
How many of 20 sampled answers will contain a word with a 30 percent probability?
Does the temperature change what the model knows, or only how it chooses?
commonMisconceptions: A language model always gives the same answer to the same words.
A higher temperature makes the model more accurate or more creative without cost.
If the most likely word is correct, the model will never say the wrong one.
Temperature changes what the model knows, rather than how it chooses.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on five challenge questions (mastery: 4 of 5).
Explain why the same question can get different answers on different days.
